summary: Berthe Jansen works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA and PhD at Leiden University under Jonathan A. Silk and an MPhil at Oxford, later serving as assistant professor at Leiden (2015–2016) and research fellow at Heidelberg (~2015–2016).

A linguist and Indologist, Delbrück completed his Promotion at Berlin and Habilitation at Halle under Pott, Weber, and Bopp. He taught at Gymnasium Marienwerder (1864–1866) and Halle (1867–1870) before serving as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Jena (1870–1913).

Working in Sinology, Tibetology, and Central Asian studies, Laufer studied at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady (PhD). He held positions at the American Museum of Natural History, lectured at Columbia (1905–1907), and became curator at the Field Museum in 1907.

Beru Khyentse Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He received traditional training under teachers including Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Kalu Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

An Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar, Bäumer earned her doctorate at Munich and studied under Lakshman Joo. She held posts at Banaras Hindu University, the Alice Boner Institute, Vienna, IGNCA, and the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

An Indologist and philosopher, Heimann earned doctorates at Strasbourg and Kiel and habilitated at Halle under Eugen Hultzsch. She taught at Halle, became associate professor at Hamburg, and held appointments at the universities of London, Oxford, and Colombo.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

A linguist and Indologist, Krishnamurti earned his AM and PhD at Pennsylvania and studied under Murray B. Emeneau. He taught at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (where he was professor 1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad (1986–1999).

A scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, Das earned an MA at the University of Calcutta. He co-founded Banaras Hindu University, served on its managing board (~1916), and was headmaster of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1921–1926).
Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi is an Indologist and linguist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, including serving as head of its Research Department (attested 1989).

Dash specialized in Indology and Tibetology, studying at Gujarat Ayurved University, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi, where he completed an MA and PhD. He served as a bibliographer and cataloguer at the Library of Congress.

Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He was an honorary member of the Royal Asiatic Society and a fellow of the University of Mumbai (1882).

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ghosh served as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and as an editorial board member for the Bulletin of Tibetology (both attested 1994).

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held positions at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan (1991).
Bhau Daji Lad was an Indologist and historian who pursued his studies at Elphinstone College (~1840–1843) and Grant Medical College (~1845–1850).

A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, Anālayo completed a PhD at Ceylon and Habilitation at Marburg. His academic career includes positions at Hamburg, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy, and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Bodhi earned a BA at Brooklyn College and a PhD at Claremont Graduate University, studying under Balangoda Ananda Maitreya and Nyanaponika Thera. He edited for the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and presided over BAUS (2013).

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Pāsādika earned degrees from Magadh and Punjabi universities. He held academic posts at Punjabi University, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences, Marburg, Würzburg, and Bochum, and directed the Frankfurt Buddhist Academy in 2022.
Bhikshuni Longlian was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Fazun beginning in 1939 and also trained under traditional teacher Nenghai Shi.

Bhogilal Sandesara was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (~1940–1950). He served as Head of the Gujarati Department at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda from ~1951 to 1975.
